g.data-info: MacBook: QGroundControl for setup and monitoring (over USB-C or the radio), and mavcontrol.py, the Python + pygame program that flies the drone
SiK telemetry radio V5, ground module (from the Pixhawk kit): 433 MHz, 100 mW, USB on the Mac — mavcontrol.py opens it as /dev/tty.usbserial-0001 at 57 600 baud

g.text: No RC transmitter: the drone is flown

g.data-info: Motor 1 of the Quad X layout (front-right, CCW): A2212 13T 1000KV brushless outrunner with a 1045 propeller
ESC of motor 1: 30 A brushless ESC (SimonK-type) with a 5 V / 2 A BEC, in heat-shrink; its power leads end in crimped brass bullet connectors mated to XT60 connectors on the plate (nothing soldered)
Motor 2 of the Quad X layout (rear-left, CCW): A2212 13T 1000KV brushless outrunner with a 1045 propeller
ESC of motor 2: 30 A brushless ESC (SimonK-type) with a 5 V / 2 A BEC, in heat-shrink; its power leads end in crimped brass bullet connectors mated to XT60 connectors on the plate (nothing soldered)
Motor 3 of the Quad X layout (front-left, CW): A2212 13T 1000KV brushless outrunner with a 1045 propeller
ESC of motor 3: 30 A brushless ESC (SimonK-type) with a 5 V / 2 A BEC, in heat-shrink; its power leads end in crimped brass bullet connectors mated to XT60 connectors on the plate (nothing soldered)
Motor 4 of the Quad X layout (rear-right, CW): A2212 13T 1000KV brushless outrunner with a 1045 propeller
ESC of motor 4: 30 A brushless ESC (SimonK-type) with a 5 V / 2 A BEC, in heat-shrink; its power leads end in crimped brass bullet connectors mated to XT60 connectors on the plate (nothing soldered)

g.text: each output really drives: the numbers
printed on this board's MAIN OUT rail
do not match the firmware outputs

g.data-info: F450 bottom plate: the frame's power distribution board (black PCB with copper pads), pre-soldered; the ESCs plug into it through XT60 and crimped brass bullet connectors (nothing soldered on this build)
g.text: F450 bottom plate = power distribution board (+ / −)

g.data-info: Pixhawk PRO flight controller: STM32F4 @ 168 MHz, 2 MB flash (FMUv3-class), running ArduCopter 4.6.3
SPKT/DSM: Spektrum satellite receiver input (unused)
BUZZER port: the buzzer from the kit
TELEM 2 = SERIAL2: MAVLink 2 to the Raspberry Pi at 57 600 baud (SERIAL2_PROTOCOL = 2, SERIAL2_BAUD = 57); its 5 V pin also powers the Pi
SWITCH port: safety switch (must be pressed before arming)
SERIAL 4/5 (unused)
TELEM 1 = SERIAL1: the SiK telemetry radio (air module)
GPS port: u-blox M8N over UART (6-pin cable)
USB (GH connector, unused; the side USB-C is used for setup)
ADC 3.3 V input (unused)
CAN bus (unused)
SPI (unused)
I2C port: the M8N module's compass (4-pin cable)
POWER port: 6-pin lead from the PM02 — 5.2 V supply plus battery voltage and current sensing
ADC 6.6 V input (unused)
Raspberry Pi 4 Model B, 2 GB: companion computer running MAVProxy / pymavlink, linked to the Pixhawk over UART (TELEM 2) and powered from the same connector's 5 V pin

g.text: Powered from the Pixhawk's TELEM 2 5 V pin (via the PM02)

g.data-info: SiK telemetry radio V5, air module (from the Pixhawk kit): 433 MHz, 100 mW, on TELEM 1; carries MAVLink between the Mac and the Pixhawk
PM02 V3.2 power module (kit): 2–12S input, 5.2 V / 3 A output to the flight controller, voltage and current sensing; XT60 in and out — battery settings never configured in QGroundControl
LiPo 3S 11.1 V, 3000 mAh, 35C, XT60 (AMZZN) — stored in a LiPo-safe bag
Buzzer (kit): arming and status tones
Safety switch (kit): must be pressed before the motors can be armed; its LED ring blinks until then
u-blox M8N GPS + compass module on its mast (kit): GPS over UART, compass over I2C; no GPS fix indoors
QGroundControl on the Mac: firmware (ArduCopter 4.6.3), calibrations, parameters and monitoring, over USB-C or the telemetry link
mavcontrol.py (Python + pygame): arm / disarm, take-off, land, throttle and mode keys, RC override of the throttle channel at 10 Hz, live monitor of attitude, yaw rate and motor PWM
ArduCopter 4.6.3 (fmuv3 build) on the Pixhawk PRO: Quad X; SERIAL2_PROTOCOL = 2, SERIAL2_BAUD = 57; arming checks for RC and GPS disabled, FS_THR_ENABLE = 0, DISARM_DELAY = 0
g.text: RC + GPS arming checks off · FS_THR 0 · DISARM_DELAY 0

g.data-info: On the Pi: Raspberry Pi OS 32-bit, MAVProxy and pymavlink in a virtual environment (~/mavlink_project/venv), started by hand over SSH: mavproxy.py --master=/dev/serial0 --baudrate 57600
g.text: /dev/serial0 @ 57 600 baud · started by hand over SSH

path.data-info: ESC 1 → motor: three phase wires on brass bullet connectors (crimped, not soldered); swapping two reverses the spin
Plate → ESC 1: battery voltage (+ / −)
ESC 2 → motor: three phase wires on brass bullet connectors (crimped, not soldered); swapping two reverses the spin
Plate → ESC 2: battery voltage (+ / −)
ESC 3 → motor: three phase wires on brass bullet connectors (crimped, not soldered); swapping two reverses the spin
Plate → ESC 3: battery voltage (+ / −)
ESC 4 → motor: three phase wires on brass bullet connectors (crimped, not soldered); swapping two reverses the spin
Plate → ESC 4: battery voltage (+ / −)
TELEM 2 5 V pin → Pi pin 2 (5 V): the Pi is powered by the flight controller's 5 V rail
Battery → PM02 (XT60)
PM02 6-pin lead → POWER port: 5.2 V supply + battery voltage / current sensing
PM02 XT60 out → F450 plate: main battery current to the ESCs
MAIN OUT → ESC 1: PWM servo lead (signal + ground); which motor each output drives is set by SERVOn_FUNCTION (the pin numbers printed on this board do not match the firmware outputs)
MAIN OUT → ESC 2: PWM servo lead (signal + ground); which motor each output drives is set by SERVOn_FUNCTION (the pin numbers printed on this board do not match the firmware outputs)
MAIN OUT → ESC 3: PWM servo lead (signal + ground); which motor each output drives is set by SERVOn_FUNCTION (the pin numbers printed on this board do not match the firmware outputs)
MAIN OUT → ESC 4: PWM servo lead (signal + ground); which motor each output drives is set by SERVOn_FUNCTION (the pin numbers printed on this board do not match the firmware outputs)
Pi UART (pin 8 TXD → TELEM2 RX, pin 10 RXD ← TELEM2 TX, pin 6 GND) ↔ Pixhawk TELEM 2: MAVLink 2 at 57 600 baud

g.text: UART · MAVLink 2 · 57 600 baud (red: 5 V to the Pi)

path.data-info: Air radio → TELEM 1 (6-pin GH cable): MAVLink
Buzzer → BUZZER port
Safety switch → SWITCH port
M8N GPS → GPS port (UART, 6-pin)
M8N compass → I2C port (4-pin)
USB: ground radio on the Mac
Wi-Fi: the Mac reaches the Pi over SSH on the home network
433 MHz link between the two SiK radios: MAVLink from mavcontrol.py / QGroundControl to the Pixhawk
